A1.justification: Both 17-page PDFs describe the same SLoW research. Their text, equations, figures, ten tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite table relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original FLORES translation experiments with ChatGPT, Llama and DeepSeek-V3, including quantitative comparisons, dictionary-selection analyses and translation case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the quantitative comparisons and case studies redistributed between the main paper and appendix.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same frequency-based dictionary selection, frequency estimation, dictionary construction and translation prompts. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same FLORES language coverage and into-English, from-English and non-English-centric translation scenarios. The appendix language-class and language-pair tables are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same vanilla, PoS-based, Differ in Round-trip, Differ in Translation, full-dictionary and high-frequency baselines. GPT/ChatGPT and Llama/LLaMa label edits do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Both sample 200 FLORES devtest instances, use BLEU, chrF and wmt22-comet-da, and align dictionary budgets with Differ in Round-trip. Adding the 671B designation documents the retained DeepSeek-V3 model rather than establishing a configuration change.

E4.justification: The PoS analysis, full-dictionary and high-frequency comparisons, and both translation case studies are retained. The Tsonga case study moves from v1 Table 7 to v2 Table 3; it is not newly added evidence.

E5.justification: Both retain the same descriptive counts and percentages. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests, and no uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All ten matched tables retain their numerical entries, and Figures 1–2 retain identical plotted data. For example, v1 Table 8's BLEU/chrF results reappear unchanged as v2 Table 4. The case-study translations and scores also match.

T1.justification: Section 3's conditional-generation likelihood, ADS formulation and frequency-selection equation remain unchanged. No substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list preserve the ADS task, SLoW method, token/performance trade-off and claimed advantages, including occasionally outperforming full dictionaries. Conclusion edits do not change these claims.

C2.justification: v1 identifies limited language coverage and proposes expansion. v2 additionally states that suitable datasets are lacking and collection is difficult, explaining a constraint on expansion. Existing result interpretations and other limitations remain.

D1.justification: The first-page promise of code and data upon publication is replaced by a specific project repository URL. Section 4.2 additionally identifies DeepSeek-V3 as 671B. These improve documentation; the PDFs do not establish the repository's accessibility or contents.

R1.justification: v2 adds eight references, including TRIP, CLEAN-EVAL, LNE-blocking and Adam's Law. Section 2 briefly mentions subsequent sentence-level frequency work. These additions expand context without substantially redefining ADS's research positioning.

P1.justification: Limited edits affect the introduction, conclusion, limitations, author affiliation, notation and model-name capitalization. Cross-references follow table renumbering, while the section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing tables are relocated and renumbered, notably v1 Tables 7–8 becoming v2 Tables 3–4 among the reference pages. Prompt boxes receive rounded, shaded styling, and appendix material is consolidated. Figure designs and table structures remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reproducibility documentation through a concrete repository address and explicit DeepSeek-V3 size, and clarifies the dataset barrier to broader language coverage. Empirical support remains unchanged. These limited gains are tempered by relocated tables interrupting the references and figure captions still describing Table 4 as an appendix table.
